gamma_events.title: Highest temperature in Munich on September 1?
gamma_events.description:
This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Munich Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 1 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eddm

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from multiple models positions 25°C as the most probable daily maximum for Munich on September 2, 2026, with 26°C a close secondary outcome.** Short-range guidance, including GFS-based outputs and European sources such as Meteoblue and Yr.no, shows afternoon peaks of 24–26°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies. High pressure associated with an Azores high extension maintains a moderate westerly flow of Atlantic air, limiting both strong warming and significant cloud cover that would suppress temperatures.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus from multiple models positions 25°C as the most probable daily maximum for Munich on September 2, 2026, with 26°C a close secondary outcome.** Short-range guidance, including GFS-based outputs and European sources such as Meteoblue and Yr.no, shows afternoon peaks of 24–26°C under partly to mostly cloudy skies. High pressure associated with an Azores high extension maintains a moderate westerly flow of Atlantic air, limiting both strong warming and significant cloud cover that would suppress temperatures.

Observed model agreement is tight for this 24-hour lead time, with limited spread reflecting typical uncertainty ranges in boundary-layer mixing and insolation under variable cloud. Historical climatology for early September (average high ~22°C) provides context that current conditions sit modestly above normal but well below record levels. No major forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24–48 hours, supporting the market-implied odds that heavily favor 25°C while assigning meaningful but secondary probability to 26°C. Updated model runs and official DWD guidance expected overnight will be the next key inputs for any probability adjustment.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the London City Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=eglc

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent Met Office and model guidance for September 2 point to a mostly cloudy day with southwesterly flow, light morning rain risk, and afternoon brighter spells that limit surface heating. Official forecasts converge on a maximum of 21–23 °C, with many runs peaking near 21 °C under widespread cloud and modest wind speeds that enhance mixing and suppress further warming. Early-September climatology places the London mean daily maximum near 20–22 °C, so current conditions align closely with the seasonal norm rather than any anomalous ridge or warm advection. Updated model runs released overnight on September 1 reinforced the 21 °C outcome as the modal solution, prompting the market’s heavy weighting toward that bin while leaving modest probability for a 22 °C nudge if afternoon sun breaks through more than expected. No major forecast shifts have occurred in the past 24 hours to alter this consensus.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from sources including WeatherBug and WindBorne currently project a high of 83–84°F for New York City on September 3, 2026, with a 70–90% chance of showers or thunderstorms, southwest winds of 5–10 mph, and high humidity.** This aligns closely with the market’s leading outcomes (84–85°F at 35.5%, 86–87°F at 20.5%, and 82–83°F at 20%), which together capture over 75% of trader-implied probability.

The primary scientific drivers include an incoming warm, moist air mass ahead of a weak frontal boundary. Southwest flow advects humid air from the south, supporting surface temperatures in the low-to-mid 80s, while widespread cloud cover and precipitation reduce solar insolation and cap daytime heating near or slightly above the seasonal average high of 80.2°F. Model consensus shows limited spread, with most runs clustering in the 82–85°F range; any breaks in clouds or delayed rain could push readings toward 86°F, while heavier or earlier precipitation would favor the lower end of that band.

Recent observations from September 2—persistent rain, highs only in the mid-70s, and dew points near 70°F—reinforce the setup for continued warmth without extreme heat. Traders appear to be weighting the latest model runs and official guidance (NHC/NOAA analogs for early-September patterns), producing tight clustering around the most probable temperature bins rather than outliers. Updated forecast packages expected overnight or early on September 3 represent the next key data point that could shift these implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from sources including WeatherBug and WindBorne currently project a high of 83–84°F for New York City on September 3, 2026, with a 70–90% chance of showers or thunderstorms, southwest winds of 5–10 mph, and high humidity.** This aligns closely with the market’s leading outcomes (84–85°F at 35.5%, 86–87°F at 20.5%, and 82–83°F at 20%), which together capture over 75% of trader-implied probability.

The primary scientific drivers include an incoming warm, moist air mass ahead of a weak frontal boundary. Southwest flow advects humid air from the south, supporting surface temperatures in the low-to-mid 80s, while widespread cloud cover and precipitation reduce solar insolation and cap daytime heating near or slightly above the seasonal average high of 80.2°F. Model consensus shows limited spread, with most runs clustering in the 82–85°F range; any breaks in clouds or delayed rain could push readings toward 86°F, while heavier or earlier precipitation would favor the lower end of that band.

Recent observations from September 2—persistent rain, highs only in the mid-70s, and dew points near 70°F—reinforce the setup for continued warmth without extreme heat. Traders appear to be weighting the latest model runs and official guidance (NHC/NOAA analogs for early-September patterns), producing tight clustering around the most probable temperature bins rather than outliers. Updated forecast packages expected overnight or early on September 3 represent the next key data point that could shift these implied probabilities.

This consensus, combined with observed midday readings near 31°C and limited cooling from scattered showers, underpins the market’s strong weighting toward 31°C as the most probable outcome. Lower probabilities for 30°C or 32°C reflect minor model spread in boundary-layer mixing and precipitation timing, while extremes above 33°C or below 29°C remain unlikely given stable large-scale conditions and historical early-September climatology. Traders appear to be pricing in official guidance updates through the afternoon observation window.
